title: "Dario is hyping the dangers so OSS models are illegal and he stays in control"
titleZh: "Dario is hyping the dangers so OSS models are illegal and he stays in control"
author: MrBuddyCasino
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: PostPostYann LeCun on X: "Dario's spiel since GPT-2 has always been about hyping the dangers so that open models would be made illegal and *he* would stay in control. He left OpenAI because he wasn't going to have control. It's like the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic so they would keep in control of the dogma. It stops the population from freely accessing diverse knowledge. It's a new form of medieval obscurantism."Conversation

children.author: DrScientist
children.textRawHtml:
Why? I'd contend it is based on a false premise - that secure digital comms is at the heart of crime and terrorism.

If I look at domestic terrorism events in the UK - most appear to have been done by individuals inspired by an idea rather than being part of some secret organisation held together by encrypted comms.

Likewise crime is either out of desperation, haphazard or done by people with severe problems.

Organised crime on the other hand requires both trust and fear, the sort that uses in person meetings to build and maintain.

I'd turn the 'if you have nothing to hide, why worry' argument on it's head.

If you have a reason to worry, why use digital encrption comms - when you can just meet in person or use very simple pre-agreed code phrases etc?

I accept that you can use mass surveillance to pick up suspicious behaviour of those lone terrorists ( internet history, purchase history etc ) - however such a tool in the wrong hands is much more dangerous than a few individuals in my view.

children.author: jdietrich
children.textRawHtml:
The most successful police operation against organised crime in British history came about as a result of compromising an encrypted chat network. Pretending that end-to-end encryption isn't massively useful to criminals is just silly - a more serious argument would be that the benefits outweigh the harms, or that the right to privacy is absolute.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EncroChat

children.author: Anvoker
children.textRawHtml:
The way we keep, intentionally or unintentionally framing the problem as a simple tradeoff to be rationally investigated warps the whole discourse. I do not accuse you of doing anything wrong, but this seemingly neutral framing is not neutral at all in practice.

When you frame things this way people have a strong tendency to give up more and more for safety as long as they are not obviously and immediately affected (or when the obviously and immediately affected population is a minority).

It's death by a thousand cuts to liberties that end up shaping society in a deep manner.

children.author: mrngld
children.textRawHtml:
I agree with you about banning things. But if you're talking about Dario, etc., he's got a right to his own opinion, and companies are simply groups of people. That you've got Nvidia and Anthropic, Jensen the White and Dario the Dark, saying opposite things is perfectly fine and should be viewed as healthy.

What wouldn't be healthy is if one of the aligned groups could silence others. Or if anyone took these companies opinions for more than what they are, since obviously they have varied interests (including making money). But that's true of individuals opinions as well, everyone has mixed motives. Part of being an adult is discernment.
